label: Vāta
title: Vāta
html:
Vāta is the breath of movement — light, airy, and forever in motion, like wind moving through the world. You'll know Vāta by its lightness. The body is thin and slender, tall or small, its bones close to the surface and its proportions delicate. Weight never lingers here. The face is fine and angular, the eyes small and quick, always darting toward the next thing. The skin runs dry, the hair dry and curling. And everything about Vāta hurries — quick steps, restless hands, words that tumble out fast. At its best, this restless energy becomes creativity, joy, and a mind open to anything. But when the wind blows too hard, it scatters — into fear, worry, and thoughts that won't settle.

Vāta — the principle of movement

Vāta Dosha is the Ayurvedic principle of mobility that regulates all activity in the body and mind, from the flow of thoughts to the movement of food through the intestines. It governs all biological movement and carries the other two Doshas throughout the body. It is primarily composed of the Ākāsha (ether) and Vāyu (air) elements.

Vāta’s Gunas

  • Rūksha dry: leading to dry skin, hair, lips, tongue, colon, tending toward constipation and a hoarse voice
  • Laghu light: light muscles, bones, thin body frame, light sleep and being underweight
  • Shīta cold: resulting in cold hands and feet, poor circulation, dislike for cold environments prefers hot, tending toward stiffness of muscles
  • Khāra rough: characterized by rough, cracked skin, nails, hair, teeth, hands and feet, and cracking joints
  • Sūkshma subtle: associated with subtle fear, anxiety, insecurity, goose-bumps, muscle twitching, and fine tremors
  • Chala mobile: leading to fast walking and talking, doing many things at a time, restless eyes, hands, and feet, unstable joints, many dreams, loves travelling and does not stay at one place, swinging moods, shaky faith, scattered mind
  • Vishada clear: clairvoyant; understands immediately and forgets immediately; clear, empty mind, experiences void and loneliness

Vāta’s physical appearance, Ākruti is typically

  • body frame: thin, slender, often disproportionate; very tall or very short, with visible bones and prominent veins
  • weight: generally low or underweight, with difficulty gaining weight
  • nose: often thin, crooked, or uneven, may have a deviated septum
  • eyes: small, sunken, dry, and active, the gaze is unsteady or darting, iris is dark, gray, or brown
  • lips: thin, dry, and cracked, often with a brownish color tinge
  • teeth: long, protruding, or irregular, with gaps between them, big thin gums
  • skin: thin, dry, cold, and rough to the touch, tends to a darker complexion and tans easily
  • hair: dry, brittle, curly or kinky; thin or scarce and prone to split ends and dandruff
  • nails: dry, brittle, rough, break easily and may have grooves

Vāta’s physiology and behavior

  • digestion and appetite: Vishama Āgni, irregular digestion, with gas and bloating and a tendency to constipation, variable appetite
  • sleep: light, interrupted sleep, especially in cold or noisy places
  • speech: fast, spontaneous, sometimes slurred or disorganized
  • psychology: when balanced, creative, joyful, and flexible. When imbalanced, prone to fear, anxiety, insecurity, restlessness, and indecision
  • pulse: Sarpa moving like a snake, fast, feeble, cold, and thin, felt best under the index finger
  • dreams: active and frequent, often of falling, flying, or being attacked

label: Pitta
title: Pitta
html:
Pitta is the fire within — heat and intensity, the spark that transforms food into energy and ideas into action. You'll know Pitta by its strength. The body is medium and well-built, muscled and steady, holding its shape with ease. The face tapers to a point, cheeks flushed with warmth, the nose sharp, the eyes bright and quick to squint in the light. The skin is fair and easily reddened, scattered with freckles, and the fine hair often greys before its time. At its best, this fire becomes intelligence, discipline, and the courage to lead. But when the flames rise too high, they burn — into anger, impatience, and a perfectionism that spares no one.

Pitta — the principle of transformation

Pitta Dosha is the Ayurvedic principle of transformation that regulates metabolism, digestion, and the conversion of energy throughout the body and mind. Primarily composed of the Āgni (fire) and Āpas (water) elements, it manifests as the heat and biochemical actions required for life.

Pitta’s Gunas

  • Ushna hot: good digestive fire, strong appetite, body temperature tends to be higher than average, dislikes heat tends toward gray hair with receding hair line or baldness, soft brown hair on the body and face
  • Tikshna sharp: sharp teeth, distinct eyes, pointed nose, tapering chin, heart-shaped face, good absorption and digestion, sharp memory and understanding, intolerance of hard work, irritable, intellectual mind
  • Laghu light: light to medium body frame, does not tolerate bright light, fair, shiny skin, bright eyes
  • Drava liquid: loose liquid stools, soft delicate muscles, excess urine, sweat and thirst
  • Snigdha oily: soft, oily skin, hair and feces, difficulty digesting deep-fried foods, which may cause headache
  • Sara spreading: spreads as rash, acne, or inflammation over the body or affected areas, Pitta wants to spread their name and fame all over the world

Pitta’s physical appearance, Ākruti is typically

  • body frame: medium and well-proportioned, with good musculature and moderate strength
  • weight: moderate and stable; seldom gains or loses much
  • face: often heart-shaped, tapering, or triangular, with rosy or reddish cheeks
  • nose: medium-sized, sharp, and straight, often with a reddish tip
  • eyes: moderate, bright, and sharp; light-colored iris (gray, green, hazel, or yellowish), sensitive to light
  • lips: soft, thin, and pinkish or reddish
  • teeth: medium-sized, often yellowish or sharp; gums tender and prone to bleeding
  • skin: warm, oily, and sensitive; fair with a coppery or reddish complexion, prone to freckles, moles, acne, and sunburn
  • hair: straight, fine, and oily; soft brown, blond, or reddish, prone to premature graying or balding
  • nails: pink, flexible, lustrous, and sharp

Pitta’s physiology and behavior

  • digestion and appetite: Tikshna Āgni, very strong and fast digestion that can cause heartburn or acid reflux, they become irritable if they do not eat on time
  • sleep: sound but moderate; may wake near midnight or 2 AM with a burst of energy.
  • speech: sharp, clear, distinct, and often authoritative or inspiring.
  • psychology: when balanced, intelligent, disciplined, and courageous leaders. When imbalanced, prone to anger, irritability, jealousy, judgment, and perfectionism.
  • pulse: Manduka moving like a frog jumping, bounding, hot, and forceful, felt best under the middle finger
  • dreams: fiery or intellectual, problem-solving, teaching, exams, fire, or violence

label: Kapha
title: Kapha
html:
Kapha is the earth beneath it all — water and soil, the steady force that gives the body form and holds it together. You'll know Kapha by its solidity. The body is broad and strong, built on a generous frame, and weight settles here and stays. The face is large and round as the moon, the cheeks full, the eyes big and gentle beneath thick lashes. The skin is cool, soft, and slow to age; the hair thick and lustrous through the years. Kapha moves without hurry, calm and deep and unshakable. At its best, this steadiness becomes love, compassion, and a forgiving heart. But when the earth grows too heavy, it clings — to comfort, to possessions, to a stillness that won't move.

Kapha — the principle of structure

Kapha Dosha is the Ayurvedic principle of structure, lubrication, and cohesion that gives the body physical form and stability. It is the “glue” that holds the cells together and supplies the water for all bodily systems and joints. It is primarily composed of the Āpas (water) and Prthivī (earth) elements.

Kapha’s Gunas

  • Guru heavy: heavy bones, muscles, and large body frame, tends to be overweight, grounded, and has deep heavy voice
  • Manda slow/dull: slow walk, talk, digestion, and metabolism, overall sluggish gestures
  • Hima cool: cool clammy skin, steady appetite and thirst with slow metabolism and digestion, repeated cold, congestion, and cough
  • Snigdha oily: oily skin, hair and feces, lubricated, unctuous joints and organs
  • Drava liquid: excess salivation, congestion in the chest, sinuses, throat and head
  • Shlakshna slimy/smooth: smoothness of the skin and organs, smooth and gentle mind, calm nature
  • Sandra dense: dense pad of fat, thick skin, hair, nail and feces, plump rounded organs, firmness and solidity of muscles, compact, condensed tissues
  • Mrudu soft: soft pleasing look and skin, and a gentle, caring personality, love, compassion, kindness and forgiveness
  • Sthira stable/static: stability and a preference for sedentary activities loves sitting, sleeping and doing nothing
  • Picchila sticky: cohesive quality causes compactness, firmness of joints, and organs; loves to hug, is deeply attached in love and relationships
  • Āvila cloudy: early morning cloudy mind and fogginess, often desires coffee as a stimulant to start the day
  • Kathina hard: firm muscles, strength, rigid attitude
  • Sthūla gross: visible structures and the potential for obesity

Kapha’s physical appearance, Ākruti is typically

  • body frame: big, broad, and strong, with a large skeletal structure
  • weight: generally heavy; gains weight easily and finds it hard to lose
  • face: large, round, and attractive, with a “moon-shaped” look and plump cheeks
  • nose: large, wide, and thick; may be short and button-like
  • eyes: big, round, and beautiful, with long, thick lashes; iris blue, light gray, or black; very white sclera
  • lips: large, full, soft, and oily, often pale
  • teeth: large, strong, and white, regularly spaced, with strong gums
  • skin: thick, cool, soft, and oily; fair or pale, ages slowly and looks younger than its age
  • hair: thick, luxuriant, wavy, and oily; abundant and healthy even in old age
  • nails: strong, thick, smooth, and symmetrical, with a polished look

Kapha’s physiology and behavior

  • digestion and appetite: Manda Āgni slow but steady, prolonged digestion, with a feeling of heaviness or fullness
  • sleep: deep, sound, and prolonged; falls asleep easily and is hard to wake.
  • speech: slow, melodious, and monotonous, with a deep, voluminous voice.
  • psychology: when balanced, loving, compassionate, and forgiving. When imbalanced, prone to greed, attachment, possessiveness, and lethargy.
  • pulse: Hamsa moving like a swan, slow, deep, and wavy, felt best under the ring finger
  • dreams: romantic and watery—lakes, oceans, swimming, snow, or ducks.
